title: Statutory interpretation: text, purpose and the canons
question: How do courts decide what a statute means?

steps.note: A statute read against its purpose and the maxim that no one profits from his own wrong.
Letter versus spirit: the Court reads an exception into a clear text.
Lenity and ordinary meaning: an airplane is not a “vehicle”.
Legislative history used to narrow a broad statutory term.
Avoidance and absurdity: “utilized” read narrowly to keep a statute constitutional.
Noscitur a sociis and reading a term consistently through the whole Act.
The presumption that Congress legislates with domestic concerns in mind.
Harmonizing two statutes rather than finding a repeal by implication.
Textualism with a diagram: a bump stock is not a machine gun.
Ordinary meaning covers a weapon parts kit that is readily convertible.
